subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` keys that look like credentials be allowed into skill-owned host `exec` subprocesses, and what scoping prevents leakage into unrelated generic exec?
rationale: The current code violates the documented host skill-env behavior for real users, but changing it decides when credential values may enter executable child-process environments.

options.title: Allow skill-scoped exec env
options.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

options.title: Require metadata declarations
options.body: Keep credential-shaped names blocked unless the skill metadata declares them, then update the affected skill metadata or package docs for this credential path.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Document that credential-shaped per-skill env names are intentionally blocked and require top-level, system, or sandbox-specific env configuration instead.

recommendation.title: Allow skill-scoped exec env
recommendation.body: Permit user-configured per-skill env keys for that skill's own host exec context while keeping dangerous env names blocked and stripping skill secrets from unrelated generic exec.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses security policy, host env sanitization, and credential-to-exec behavior where steipete has strong adjacent history.
